chapter: Bix, Trumbauer and the Goldkette sidemen
title: Bix's drinking and the band's drinking and spitballs
summary: They discuss how Bix's drinking affected his playing, and how the whole band drank and acted like kids, driving Virginia's father to leave.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: You said something earlier about his drinking. When he was drinking a lot, did it show in the way he played? Could you tell?
Sure.
You could tell. He played differently when he was not sober.
Yeah.
He would be a little late coming in, and things like that.
Okay. Did any of that show up in the records?
I don't think so.
Because I'm not aware of that.
Not to my knowledge.
I'm not aware of that either.
No, I think that...
Russ Morgan was leading the band, How did Russ Morgan feel about his drinking? Did that bother him?
No, it didn't bother him.
They all drank quite a bit.
They all drank.
Yes.
It wasn't just one.
The whole group. When my father went back to Chicago, he couldn't stand it.
He couldn't stand all the drinking.
No. Because they weren't serious enough.
Well Bix was very serious. But he was also serious about drinking.
Yeah.
When they began on the stand to rehearse, they would cut up and they would throw spitballs.
Oh boy. Did Bix act that way too?
Yeah, everybody in the band.
Like a bunch of kids.
But they were a bunch of kids.
They were in their twenties.
Everybody in the band.
Was a kid. And they'd smack one another and I don't know, just cut up.
Everybody went nuts.
Everyone nuts. They weren't too mature.
No, they weren't.
My father was bald and he tore out the rest of his hair, I think.
Is that right?
He just left it. He just voluntary...
